parole.testo: A Persian form of Ancient Greek συρικόν (surikón, “red lead”) (also found as Latin syricum), synonym of σάνδυξ (sándux). Doublet of زَرْقُون (zarqūn).
Developed from Arabic تُرْس (turs, “shield”), from Persian ترس (tors, “shield”), from Ancient Greek θυρεός (thureós).

parole.significato: tharid (Arab dish of bread in broth)
parole.testo: From Persian ترید (tarid, “a soup”), apparently in a variant as ثَلْجَم (ṯaljam), and possibly ultimately from a diminutive of Ancient Greek ἴτριον (ítrion), hence doublet of إِطْرِيَة (ʔiṭriya).
From Persian گمست (gamast), ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀμέθυστος (améthustos, “not drunk”), from ἀ- (a-, “not”) + μεθύω (methúō, “I am drunk”), from μέθυ (méthu, “wine”).

parole.significato: the name of certain purgative spurges, particularly Croton tiglium, and also Euphorbia dendroides, Euphorbia lathyris,…
parole.testo: From Persian دند (dand, “tooth; Croton tiglium”), clipped from دندان (dandân, “tooth; Croton tiglium”). The alternative forms are influenced by Ancient Greek δενδροειδής (dendroeidḗs, “tree-like”).
From Persian شلغم (šalġam), ultimately from Ancient Greek σικελικόν (sikelikón, literally “the Sicilian one”); doublet of سِلْق (silq).

parole.significato: bugloss (Anchusa gen. et spp. and Echium spp.)
parole.testo: Calque of Persian گاوزبان (gâv-zabân) of the same meaning, itself a calque of Ancient Greek βούγλωσσον (boúglōsson).
Literally, “tongue of the lamb”. Calque of Persian زبان بره (zabân-e barre) of the same meaning, itself a calque of Ancient Greek ἀρνόγλωσσον (arnóglōsson).

parole.significato: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see لِسَان (lisān), كَلْب (kalb).
parole.testo: Calque of Persian سگزبان (sag-zabân) of the same meaning, itself a calque of Ancient Greek κυνόγλωσσον (kunóglōsson).
